events.title: Eloise May Teen Night: Hot Chocolate and Cozy Crafts
events.description: It's the season to be cozy! Grab some delicious hot chocolate and cookies and make something crafty. All materials provided. Dietary needs and restrictions are considered for this program; feel free to contact us with any requests for accommodations.

events.title: Sheridan Afterschool Club (Ages 9-12)
events.description: Get moving, make friends, and have fun! Join us each month for exciting activities like obstacle courses, giant games, challenges, and more—indoors or outside (weather permitting). All activities include options for different abilities so everyone can join in. Come play, move, and connect after school! This is a drop-in event with no registration required. Because families will be invited to enter as space allows, wait times are possible. Expect to spend about 90 minutes with us for this experience.

events.title: Music and Movement (Ages 2-5)
events.description: Drop by and join us for a fun program that will get kids singing, dancing and exploring musical instruments while also helping them develop motor and listening skills. NO REGISTRATION REQUIRED! Explore these Music and Movement books to help children learn about music and to get them up and moving!

events.title: Tween Scene (Ages 9-12)
events.description: Looking for a space that’s just for tweens? Tween Scene is a monthly hangout at Eloise May Library where kids ages 9–12 can explore their creativity, build friendships, and have fun with hands-on activities, games, and challenges. Each month features a new theme—from DIY crafts to collaborative projects—designed to spark imagination and fun! This is a drop-in event with no registration required. Because tweens will be invited to enter as space allows, wait times are possible. Expect to spend about one hour with us this experience.

events.title: Classic Game Club
events.description: Come and enjoy classic board and card games with friendly comradery with others. Join in pastimes such as Yahtzee, Sorry, Scrabble, Crazy Eights and more. Whether you’re just playing for fun or feeling competitive, this is the place for you!

events.title: Southglenn Teen Night - Bingo & Boba
events.description: Calling all Disney fans! Test your Disney knowledge and your luck with a magical night of Disney-themed Bingo. Win fun prizes, sip on delicious boba tea, and enjoy an evening filled with your favorite characters, movies, and songs. Whether you're a Disney superfan or just looking for a fun night out with friends, join us for a cozy and exciting evening of Bingo, boba, and Disney magic! ✨🧋🏰 Snacks will be provided!. This event is for teens aged 12 - 18.

events.title: Tween and Teen Movie Night: Chronicles of Narnia
events.description: Join us for the imaginatively classic film Chronicles of Narnia 2005 (Rated PG) Runtime: 143 Minutes The story follows Four British siblings - Peter, Susan, Edmund, and Lucy are evacuated to a countryside estate. While playing a game of hide-and-seek, the youngest sibling, Lucy, discovers a magical wardrobe that acts as a portal to the mystical land of Narnia. We will be in the Forum Theatre at Koelbel Library, film starts promptly at 5:00 PM

events.title: May Movie Night
events.description: Come enjoy a night of film fun for adults at Eloise May Library on the first Tuesday of every month! Popcorn and drinks will be provided. For the last movie of every quarterly theme (the movies featured in March, June, September, and December), there will be a craft kit for you to either do during the movie or take home with you! events.title: Plant Propagation | Multiplica tus plantas de interior
events.description: In this program, we will learn how to take cuttings from indoor plants to create new ones. This is an easy way to add many more plants to your home and brighten up your indoor space. We will also cover how to take care of them and what plants work best for propagating. You will also get to take one home! Spanish interpretation will be provided. To request additional language support, please contact Heidi Tingey, htingey@ald.lib.co.us, by November 20. En este programa aprenderemos a tomar esquejes de plantas de interior para crear nuevas plantas. Esta es una excelente manera de añadir más plantas a tu hogar y darle vida a tus espacios interiores. También aprenderemos cómo cuidarlas y qué plantas son las más adecuadas para propagar.¡Además podrás llevarte una a casa! Se ofrecerá interpretación en español. Para solicitar apoyo en otro idioma, comunícate con Heidi Tingey, htingey@ald.lib.co.us , antes del 20 de noviembre. DISCOVER MORE Explore these books and learn techniques for Propagating Plants and Unique Gardening . Before the event begins, we invite you to explore even more that Arapahoe Libraries has to offer. Check out our upcoming adult programs . Visit the Adults’ page to discover staff picks, career and business resources, lists and more. Browse the coming soon page.

events.title: Vitalant Blood Drive
events.description: Vitalant provides blood and special services to patients in more than 1,000 hospitals across 40 states. Millions of people in communities throughout these states depend on generous volunteer blood donors and our dedicated team to make sure lifesaving blood is available when and where it is needed. You can schedule an appointment online or Call 877-258-4825 and use the Code DEN5439 for Smoky Hill Library blood drives. Note: Drink plenty of water for 24 hours before your appointment, and eat a healthy low-fat meal within 4 hours of your donation.

events.title: Neighborhood Memory Cafe - Denver Dolls Concert
events.description: Do you have a loved one or care for someone with memory loss? This social group is just right for both of you! Get your creative juices flowing with a fun activity to complete together, explore items from the past, or learn about something new. Plus, connect with other families and browse library and community resources. Join us for a special performance by the Denver Dolls! This local trio will sing nostalgic carols and vintage music with golden harmony.

events.description: Celebrate the snowy season by making winter-themed crafts! events.title: A Culinary Journey Through Italy
events.description: Join Monica Kadillak of Kadillak Kitchens as she takes us on a journey to the tastes of Italy. Italy's cuisine is a rich tradition focused on fresh, high-quality ingredients, regional diversity and simple preparations. During this presentation, you'll sample a variety of Italian specialties while learning about the dishes and the culinary traditions behind them. Recipes & samples will be provided. Note: This event is intended for adults (ages 18+) based on the topic, material covered, or skills and tools being used. events.description: Join us to read and relax with fellow book lovers. Bring your own book or audiobook and settle into a cozy spot for an hour of quiet reading. Afterward, there will be a half hour to socialize. You can share what you’re currently reading or keep enjoying your book. For audiobook listeners, the library will provide a quiet activity, such as adult coloring pages or a puzzle, or you can bring your own. Tea and light refreshments provided.

events.title: Build Your Global Business
events.description: Learn the basics of importing, exporting and global sourcing. During this training, you will learn about: The first steps of global trade Resources for supporting international business growth in Colorado Entrepreneurs’ real-life experience creating a global business The session will end with an interactive activity where you will develop the first step for creating a global business. Light refreshments provided. Led by Sandi Moilanen, vice president of operations for World Trade Center Denver. Moilanen oversees the daily operations and programs of the organization, helps develop and implement strategic initiatives and looks for new areas of growth. She was previously the director of the Colorado International Trade Office, where she managed export promotion and foreign investment attraction activities for the State of Colorado. This event is presented by WTC Denver and Arapahoe Libraries.

events.title: Mobile Pantry at Kelver Library
events.description: Kelver Library is partnering with Food Bank of the Rockies to provide nourishing meals to our neighbors of the eastern plains community who are experiencing food insecurity. Food Bank of the Rockies will offer fresh produce, shelf-stable items and more on the second Monday of each month during 2026 at Kelver Library from 9am until the food runs out. No qualification is needed and all are welcome. This site is client choice please bring bags or boxes to transport food. Please check the Food Bank of the Rockies website for potential weather delays or closures of the distribution. Food Bank of the Rockies has more than 80 mobile pantries distributions throughout Colorado and Wyoming to reach those in need. Since mid-March, the food bank has consistently distributed more food throughout the metro and rural communities than ever before. On average, they have distributed 9 million pounds of food per month and are providing enough food to serve nearly 250,000 meals per day. To find additional food distribution locations, please visit www.foodbankrockies.org/find-food This institution is an equal opportunity provider.
